Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown to black spots with characteristic concentric rings ('target board' pattern) on older lower leaves. Leaves yellow around spots and eventually drop.
Tomato___Early_blight.causes: Fungal pathogen thriving in warm, humid weather (24-29°C) with frequent rainfall or heavy dew. Splashes from contaminated soil.
organic_treatment: Prune and destroy infected lower leaves immediately (do not compost).
Apply copper-based organic fungicides or Bacillus subtilis sprays.
Apply organic mulch around the base of plants to prevent soil splash onto foliage.
chemical_treatment: Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or azoxystrobin at the first sign of symptoms.
Rotate fungicide FRAC groups to prevent pathogen resistance.
prevention_tips: Maintain 2-3 year crop rotation away from Solanaceae family plants.
Use drip irrigation rather than overhead sprinklers to keep foliage dry.
Stake and trellis tomato plants to promote good air circulation.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked pale green to dark brown lesions on leaves and stems. White fuzzy mold often appears on leaf undersides in humid conditions.
Tomato___Late_blight.causes: Oomycete pathogen that spreads rapidly during cool, wet, and foggy weather (15-22°C). Wind-borne spores can travel miles.
organic_treatment: Remove and bag infected plants completely on dry days; do not compost.
Preventative copper soap or Bordeaux mixture applications prior to wet periods.
chemical_treatment: Apply systemic fungicides containing cymoxanil, mandipropamid, or fluopicolide.
Apply preventative protectants before forecasted rain events.
prevention_tips: Plant certified disease-free transplants and resistant cultivars (e.g., Defiant, Mountain Magic).
Destroy volunteer tomato and potato plants in the vicinity.
Ensure wide plant spacing to facilitate rapid leaf drying.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant green leaves with uniform coloration, firm texture, and no visible necrotic spots or fungal sporulation.
Tomato___healthy.causes: Optimal nutrition, appropriate watering, and healthy environmental conditions.
organic_treatment: Continue balanced organic fertilization (compost tea, well-rotted manure).
Maintain steady soil moisture.
prevention_tips: Monitor weekly for early signs of pests like aphids and hornworms.
Maintain consistent watering schedule to avoid blossom end rot.
Mulch around base to conserve moisture and suppress weeds.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green to yellowish spots on upper leaf surfaces, with olive-green to brownish velvety mold growth on the corresponding lower surfaces.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.causes: High relative humidity (>85%) and moderate temperatures (21-24°C), very common in high tunnels and greenhouses.
organic_treatment: Increase greenhouse ventilation with exhaust fans.
Apply bio-fungicides containing Trichoderma or Bacillus species.
chemical_treatment: Foliar applications of copper hydroxide or difenoconazole.
prevention_tips: Ventilate and heat greenhouses to reduce relative humidity below 80%.
Space plants generously to increase sunlight penetration.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown, angular necrotic spots on older foliage with concentric ring patterns, causing premature leaf senescence and yield reduction.
Potato___Early_blight.causes: Fungal spores overwintering in crop residue and soil, dispersed by wind, rain, and mechanical cultivation.
organic_treatment: Apply copper octanoate sprays at first symptom appearance.
Remove heavily diseased lower leaves if infestation is localized.
chemical_treatment: Sequential applications of protectants (mancozeb, chlorothalonil) or translaminar products (boscalid, pyraclostrobin).
prevention_tips: Ensure adequate nitrogen and potassium fertility; stressed plants are more susceptible.
Practice a minimum 3-year crop rotation.
Kill potato vines 2-3 weeks before harvest to prevent tuber infection.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaves turning rapidly dark brown and necrotic. In humid conditions, white fungal growth is visible on leaf margins.
Potato___Late_blight.causes: Cool, wet environmental conditions. Infected seed tubers are the primary source of initial field inoculum.
organic_treatment: Prompt destruction and disposal of infected foliage.
Fixed copper sprays applied protectively.
chemical_treatment: Apply specialized fungicides containing metalaxyl, cyazofamid, or dimethomorph according to blight forecasting models.
prevention_tips: Always use certified pathogen-free seed potatoes.
Eliminate cull piles and volunteer potatoes near production fields.
Hill potatoes well to create a soil barrier between spores and tubers.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Deep green foliage with robust stem development and no signs of chlorosis or lesion development.
Potato___healthy.causes: Healthy growing medium, balanced macronutrients, and clean seed stock.
organic_treatment: Maintain proper soil hilling to protect developing tubers from sunlight.
prevention_tips: Regular field scouting for Colorado potato beetle and aphid vectors.
Consistent soil moisture during tuber initiation and bulking stages.

Corn___Common_rust.symptoms: Oval to elongated reddish-brown to cinnamon pustules (uredinia) scattered across both upper and lower leaf surfaces. Pustules rupture the epidermis.
Corn___Common_rust.causes: Airborne spores blown northward from warmer regions, favored by moderate temperatures (16-25°C) and high humidity.
organic_treatment: Early morning scouting; generally minor in late-planted crops.
Sulfur dusts or bio-fungicides where permitted.
chemical_treatment: Triazole and strobilurin fungicides (e.g., azoxystrobin + propiconazole) if rust reaches ear leaves before dent stage.
prevention_tips: Plant rust-resistant or tolerant corn hybrids.
Plant early in the season to allow grain fill before spore arrival.

Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical grayish-green to tan lesions (cigar-shaped, 2.5 to 15 cm long) appearing first on lower leaves and progressing upward.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.causes: Overwinters in corn residue; favored by moderate temperatures (18-27°C) and prolonged wet periods.
organic_treatment: Shred and deep-plow residue after harvest to accelerate decomposition.
chemical_treatment: Foliar fungicides applied at or around VT-R1 growth stages if threshold criteria are met.
prevention_tips: Select hybrid seeds with high genetic resistance ratings (Ht genes).
Implement 1-2 year crop rotation with non-host crops like soybeans.

Corn___healthy.symptoms: Vigorous, broad green leaves with distinct parallel venation and no discoloration or necrotic streaks.
Corn___healthy.causes: Adequate nitrogen, phosphorus, and moisture balance.
organic_treatment: Side-dress with organic nitrogen sources during peak vegetative growth.
prevention_tips: Maintain soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 for optimal nutrient uptake.
Ensure proper plant population density for light interception.

Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to velvety dark brown lesions on leaves and fruit. Leaves may twist, pucker, and drop prematurely.
Apple___Apple_scab.causes: Overwinters in fallen orchard leaves; ascospores released during spring rains during bud break.
organic_treatment: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn.
Liquid lime sulfur or sulfur sprays during primary scab infection windows.
chemical_treatment: Protectant and systemic fungicides (captan, myclobutanil, or cyprodinil) timed with Mills infection periods.
prevention_tips: Plant scab-resistant cultivars (e.g., Liberty, Prima, Enterprise).
Prune tree canopy in dormant season to enhance airflow and rapid drying.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Small purple spots on leaves expanding into circular lesions with light brown centers and dark purple borders ('frogeye'). Fruit develops firm brown rot with concentric rings.
Apple___Black_rot.causes: Fungus entering through mechanical wounds, fire blight cankers, or dead wood.
organic_treatment: Prune out dead shoots, mummified fruit, and cankered branches 15 cm below infection zone.
Apply copper sprays at bud break.
chemical_treatment: Fungicide sprays including thiophanate-methyl, captan, or mancozeb from petal fall onwards.
prevention_tips: Remove all mummified apples from trees and orchard floor before spring.
Maintain tree vigor through balanced fertilization and insect pest management.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Crisp green leaves with clear serrated margins and undamaged fruit clusters.
Apple___healthy.causes: Balanced nutrition, active pest management, and clean canopy.
organic_treatment: Apply compost mulch to root zone to conserve moisture.
prevention_tips: Routine dormant oil spray for scale and mite suppression.
Install pheromone traps for codling moth monitoring.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Reddish-brown circular spots on leaves with tiny black pycnidia pimples. Berries shrivel into hard, black, wrinkled mummies.
Grape___Black_rot.causes: Overwinters in berry mummies on trellis or ground; rain splashes spores onto young tissue.
organic_treatment: Sanitation: hand-pick and dispose of all mummified grape clusters.
Preventative copper and sulfur sprays.
chemical_treatment: Myclobutanil, tebuconazole, or azoxystrobin applied from pre-bloom to 4 weeks post-bloom.
prevention_tips: Canopy management: shoot thinning and leaf pulling around fruit zone.
Ensure row orientation captures prevailing winds for maximum drying.

Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked, blistering dark spots on leaves that turn brown with yellow halos. Causes significant defoliation and sunken scabby fruit spots.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.causes: Seed-borne bacterium spreading via wind-driven rain, sprinkler irrigation, and handling wet foliage.
organic_treatment: Spray with copper hydroxide combined with potassium phosphite or bio-bactericides.
Hot water seed treatment (50°C for 25 minutes) before planting.
chemical_treatment: Copper bactericides mixed with mancozeb to overcome copper-tolerant bacterial strains.
prevention_tips: Plant only certified disease-free, tested seed and resistant bell pepper varieties.
Avoid working in pepper fields when foliage is wet.
Sanitize stakes and greenhouse trays with a 10% bleach solution between seasons.

Pepper__bell___healthy.symptoms: Glossy green leaves with intact epidermis and vigorous flowering/fruiting nodes.
Pepper__bell___healthy.causes: Optimal soil temperature (21-27°C), adequate calcium levels, and clean environment.
organic_treatment: Ensure adequate calcium nutrition to prevent blossom end rot.
prevention_tips: Maintain even soil moisture with drip irrigation.
Stake plants to support heavy fruit load.
